hook: the Benefactor, source of every benefit

segments.voice: A ride to an interview. A few minutes reading over someone's application. An introduction to the one person who knows how things work. Small things for the giver that can change a whole season for the one who gets them. Yesterday's question: Eli wants into a weekend art class, and the application asks for a portfolio and a reference. What can Amira actually give? She's a student. She can't sign anything official. Today's Name says that isn't the end of the list.

segments.voice: An-Nafi', the Benefactor, source of every benefit. It's the partner of yesterday's Name: harm and help, both in one hand. And in the Qur'an, benefit has a picture. In Surah ar-Ra'd, the chapter of thunder, rain comes down and the valleys run with it, and foam rises on top, loud and white. The foam passes away on the banks. Then, in Pickthall's words: "as for that which is of use to mankind, it remaineth in the earth." Here's the line to tell a friend tonight. In that parable, the foam is what you notice, and the water is what lasts. Usefulness stays. And notice the word: mankind. Not one group. Benefit in this verse is for people, all of them. There's also a saying reported from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that the people most beloved to God are the ones most useful to other people. So what can a student give? Help choosing the best pages. A question to her art teacher about who could write the reference. A wall in her dad's shop where the drawings can hang. None of it is official. All of it is water, not foam.

original.note: Arabic: the Benefactor, from the traditional list of the Names; said together with Ad-Darr.

trapdoor: what you thought: a God who hands out perks.

what a scholar hears: An-Nafi' is paired with Ad-Darr in the Tirmidhi list; 13:17's parable of foam and water; the 'most useful to people' saying is in at-Tabarani, graded hasan by some.
